question.text: Hariyali Foundation's FY ended 31 March. The NPO seeks to finalise (i) 60-day non-financial disclosures, (ii) the Oct-31 financial / governance pack, and (iii) the 91E AIR. Ms. Sunita Patil, SIA, is engaged for the AIR only. Which sequencing is CORRECT under LODR?

answer.text: The 60-day non-financial pack is due ~30 May; the Oct-31 pack is due by Oct 31 / ITR-due-date; the AIR follows the SEBI framework (Oct-31 or ITR-due-date, whichever later, with at least 67% program coverage).
All three must be filed on the same date (31 March + 60 days).
The AIR is due first, within 45 days of FY-end.
The Oct-31 pack is due only if the NPO has raised more than INR 5 crore.

explanation.text: The Logic: The three filings have distinct deadlines: 60-day non-financial (by ~30 May for a March year-end), Oct-31 financial / governance (or ITR-due-date whichever later), and AIR under 91E (Oct 31 or ITR-due-date whichever later for funds-raised SEs, covering at least 67% of program expenditure). They are staggered, not coincident. The Trap: Same-date filing (B), early AIR (C) and size-threshold on Oct-31 pack (D) all misread LODR. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C tests LODR result-filing sequences; XXIII extends to SSE-specific stack. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Build a three-stream Gantt on day 1 of the engagement. The SIA's AIR work-plan should start with the NPO's 60-day pack (already typically filed) because it contains the governance architecture the SIA relies on during AIR assurance.
